caption: She didn't qualify for NSFAS because we're just over the line. Would you have called the university or just paid?

slides.title:
What our daughter's
first year of varsity
costs us on R31 000 p/m
Living in Lebowakgomo
slides.body:
Him 46, her 44
Married, daughter (18) starting first year
Jobs: Municipal roads inspector & Spar bakery supervisor
Combined net: R31 000 p/m

slides.title: Bond
slides.includes: Three bedroom house, rates and levies
slides.body: We bought before she was born. It's the one number that hasn't grown.

slides.title: Varsity
slides.includes: Residence R3 100, textbooks and laptop R700, pocket money R1 400
slides.body: I said R1 000 pocket money. With Uber Eats at 11pm it's R1 900 some months. Her mother doesn't know.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Shoprite, the butcher, her bread from the bakery at cost
slides.body: It was R5 400 when she was home. I'm not saying she was the reason. She was the reason.

slides.title: Fuel
slides.includes: Two cars to two jobs, 30 km each way
slides.body: She drives the little Corsa. I drive the one that needs a service.

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: My father's care, my sister's kids
slides.body: Nobody discusses the amount. It just goes.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, electricity, car insurance, funeral policies, stokvel, phone, church
slides.body: She doesn't know the stokvel pays out in December. That money is already spoken for.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R31 000. Registration shortfalls aren't in there. Those come out of R1 780.

slides.title: We wrote it all down
slides.body:
We uploaded our statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted the transactions into categories.

Seeing 'varsity' as one number was a lot.

No bank login needed.
